newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower, Eurotunnel down.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower, Eurotunnel down.

text.p: French shares edged lower at Tuesday's open as the market consolidated recent strong gains, traders said. Some profit-taking among last week's risers was expected.
Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel requoted down 1.64 percent at nine francs in heavy trading after Monday's details of its debt restructuring. The shares were suspended on September 30.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 5.76 points or 0.27 percent at 2,145.79 at 0826 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,148 from 2,157.5 on Monday's close.
Hotelier Accor fell 18 francs to 642 as first-half net attributable profit of 104 million francs, reported on Monday, disappointed the market.
But one trader said the arrival of Jean-Marc Espalioux from Cie Generale des Eaux as Accor's management board chairman was positive as he brought a "fresh pair of eyes" to the business.
Banks BNP and Societe Generale both shed just over one percent on a view that a possible purchase of the CIC bank from insurer GAN would be a bad deal. Offers for CIC closed on Monday.
